author: Autodesk
description: A strands example illustrating how strands can be used to make an embroidery-type effect
documentation:
This graph creates and animates strands between user defined start and endpoints It could be used for embroidery type effects. ### `Shape` * **Curve Direction:**
A vector defining the direction and magnitude with which to apply the profile curve * **Curve Shape:**
A curve for defining the shape of the strands ### `Strands` * **Points per Strand:**
The number of points for each individual strand * **Duration per Strand:**
The amount of time it takes for a strand to reach its final length/shape * **Alternate Direction:**
If off, all strands grow from start points towards end points. If on, this will be alternated. * **Height Length Compensate:**
If off, the "height" of the strands will be defined solely by the "Curve Direction" and "Shape" Parameters. If on, the length of a strand is taken into account, making shorter strands more flat. ### `Animation` * **Start Frame:**
The frame at which the animation begins. * **End Frame:**
The frame at which the entire animation has finished. * **Anim Curve:**
Use this curve to change the spacing of the animation per strand. It is recommended to keep the first point at 0/0 and the last point at 1/1 and change the curve by adding new inbetween points and/or changing the interpolation type. * **Random Timing per Strand:**
When off, strands will start animating in perfect order.
When on, strands will start animating randomly.
Using this feature can make the animation longer than what has been defined under "End Frame" * **Random Min / Random Max:**
Defines the range within which start frames can be offset. Numbers are chosen randomly.
*Example*: Min -3 and Max +4 would mean a given strand startframe might be shifted earlier a maximum of 3 frames and shifted later a maximum of 4 frames. A broader Range will result in a less even pattern. * **Timing Seed:**
Changing this value will generate a different sequence of random numbers and hence alter the visual pattern. ### `Noise` * **Noise Amplitude:**
Will apply noise in the local space of each strand. This paramater controls the strength of the noise * **Noise Frequency:**
The frequency with which the noise occurs. * **Noise Curve**
Lets the user control what part of the strands will be affected by the noise * **Noise Weights (Port only)**
Another way of controlling which parts of the strands will be affected by the noise.
*Example*: The user could plug in a fractal noise field ### `Display` * **Color Min / Color Max**
Defines the range within which Strand colors are chosen. Numbers are chosen randomly. * **Color Seed**
Changing this value will generate a different sequence of random numbers and hence alter the colors chosen. * **Strand Width Factor**
A multiplier on the width of the final strand. * **Strand Width Profile**
The profile of the output width, higher numbers are wider, lower are narrower.

_notes.text:
two equal sets of points required
 here, start and end points for the 
 strands.

E M B R O I D E R 
 Main embroidery compound, 
 creates points and strands from 
 them based on input.

S T R A N D  D I S P L A Y
 All display options for the
 strands constructed in [create
 embroidery] ... the "threads"

2 SEQUENCE ARRAYS DEFINE THE START AND END FRAMES PER STRAND
IF RANDOM IS ENABLED WE RANDOMIZE THE START AND END FRAMES BASED ON USER INPUTS
THESE ARRAYS ARE PASSED INTO THE animate_value COMPOUND

THIS IS A GENERAL PURPOSE ANIMATION COMPOUND THAT LETS
THE USER ANIMATE A VALUE BASED ON START AND END FRAMES
AS WELL AS START AND END VALUES
SAMPLING AN FCURVE GIVES THE USER CONTROL SIMILAR TO KEYFRAMING
IN THE GRAPH EDITOR
THIS IS WHERE WE MOVE THE STRANDS POINTS INCREMENTALLY ALONG THE DEFINED CURVE SHAPE
THIS IS WHERE THE POINTS ARE CREATED THAT DEFINE THE STRANDS SHAPE
CREATE POINTS BTWN START AND ENDPOS
CALCULATE NOISE IN LOCAL STRANDS SPACE

APPLY FCURVE TO EACH POINT TO DEFINE SHAPE
DIRECTION OF FCURVE BASED ON USER DEFINED VECTOR
SWAP EVERY OTHER POINT TO ALTERNATE STARTING POSITION

HERE WE USE THE CROSS PRODUCT TO GET PER STRAND VECTORS/DIRECTIONS
ALONG, ACROSS, AND UP

DIVIDING THE EACH DISTANCE BY THE LONGEST DISTANCE TO GET A MULTIPLIER
FOR HEIGHT COMPENSATION. 

IF ON, THIS WILL MAKE THE SHORTER ONES FLATTER

CREATES AN ARRAY OF POINT INDICES FOR BUILDING
THE STRANDS
CREATES AN ARRAY CONTAINING THE NUMBER OF POINTS PER STRAND

PARTIAL SUMS:

FOR EXAMPLE IF ALL STRANDS HAVE 8 POINTS, THE INPUT ARRAY  IS
[8, 8, 8, 8, 8, ...]

AND THE OUTPUT
[8, 16, 24, 32, 40, ...]

ADDING ZERO AS THE FIRST ELEMENT OF THE ARRAY

EXAMPLE OUTPUT WOULD BE
[0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, ...]

THIS WILL BE FED INTO CONSTRUCT_STRANDS AND
MEANS THE FIRST STRAND WILL GO THROUGH POINT
POSITION IDs 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 
THE SECOND: 8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15 
ETC

IF NOTHING IS PLUGGED INTO "USER COLORS" THIS COMPOUND WILL CREATE RANDOM COLORS PER STRAND BASED ON THE MIN MAX VALUES
IF AN ARRAY OF COLORS IS PLUGGED INTO "USER COLORS", THOSE COLORS WILL BE APPLIED. IF THERE ARE MORE STRANDS THAN COLORS SUPPLIED
THE REMAINING STRANDS WILL BE GETTING THE DEFAULT VALUE.
IF RANDOMIZE IS ON, THE SUPPLIED COLORS WILL BE APPLIED RANDOMLY.
